name: PhoenixRepo
track: 02 The Agent That Can Explain Why
summary: Before anyone revives an abandoned GitHub repository, PhoenixRepo checks whether the idea already exists in a maintained form, and explains every refusal with evidence a reviewer can check: a quote found verbatim on the alternative's own page, and a hash-chained trace that records which model answered each call. Gate 1 judges the idea; gate 2, the revive loop, runs only on CANDIDATE.

nvidia.eligibility_path: Nemotron is called through Meterless Nightshift. Every gate-1 call requests an nvidia/nemotron-* model through Nightshift, and each LLM_CALL trace line records requested_model and the served_model that actually answered, inside the hash chain.
where_used: Problem extraction and search-query writing (fast tier, MODEL_NAME)

Every alternative-overlap judgement (fast tier, MODEL_NAME). The scored-run .env is not in the repo, and the scored v3 traces do not record temperature or thinking mode. No claim about thinking mode or temperature is made for the scored v3 run. app/agents/relevance.py sets a code default of temperature 0 and then merges the tier extra body; that default is not a record of what the scored run sent. TODO(maintainer): commit the scored-run .env, or a trace that records request_settings, before stating temperature or enable_thinking for the scored v3 run. Two requested tiers: Super for bulk checks, Ultra for the verdict. The nemotron-evidence slot says fast-tier answers used were Ultra 174 and Super-VL 18, the 16 deep-tier verdicts were served nvidia/nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b (served id; fast-tier lines request Super), and a no-tier row is Ultra 7 and Lightning 3. That slot is not a provider split.

The final gate-1 verdict (deep tier, MODEL_NAME_DEEP). The 16 deep-tier verdicts were served nvidia/nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b (served id on the nemotron-evidence deep row; the requested deep id is MODEL_NAME_DEEP). The scored traces recorded no reasoning text for the final verdict. The counter that wrote them recognised only a separate reasoning field or a complete think pair (0 of 16 in the nemotron-evidence slot), and Nightshift's answers carry reasoning inline before a bare closing think tag, so the scored traces cannot say whether the model reasoned. /ui shows a reasoning field only when the trace line contains one. The card heading is Reasoning field on this trace line.

Gate 2 part 1 only, not the scored run. The committed trace docs/rescue/trace-rescue-0xmh__fichero-printer-20261027T001117Z.jsonl (run hash 51e828e538ed8f05dda15648fc673c3461ca310a87c0af77c53482e1f0a086c4) has requested model id nvidia/nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b, served model id nvidia/nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b, and provider nvidia-direct with fallback_reason nightshift HTTP 502. Policy is PHOENIX_NEMOTRON_POLICY=fallback-nvidia; the value is not a field on the line. app/agents/relevance.py writes provider nvidia-direct only under that policy. Verified execution has never run on a real CANDIDATE. ytkb's plan (hash beginning c1d2bb22) contradicts itself and is not committed. spacer's plan was a deterministic fallback and is not committed as a model draft. The check proves a quote occurs in the cited text, not that it supports the item.
nvidia.policy: PHOENIX_NEMOTRON_POLICY: label (flag a non-Nemotron answer), require (discard it and ask again), fallback-nvidia (Nightshift first; after a Nightshift timeout, HTTP 5xx or non-Nemotron answer the same request goes to NVIDIA's API and the line is traced provider nvidia-direct). The scored run used fallback-nvidia.
nvidia.proof: python scripts/verify_trace.py logs/trace-<run_id>.jsonl --require-nemotron fails unless every answer the run used was served by nvidia/nemotron-*, and prints the count and the Nightshift / nvidia-direct split.
nvidia.measured: README.md, sections Results and Why Nemotron: Nemotron share of answers used, final-verdict answers by Nemotron, provider split, served model per provider, latency per served model. Written by scripts/fill_results.py from the scored run's report and verified traces.

meterless_runtime.role: Nightshift is the model route for gate 1, tried first on every call, and the route gate 2 requests by design. Requests are OpenAI-compatible (POST /v1/chat/completions) with meterless-app: phoenixrepo and meterless-scope: user. Routing detail returned by Nightshift (for example winning_provider and winning_model) is stored on the trace line.
meterless_runtime.probe: python scripts/nightshift_probe.py lists the nvidia/nemotron-* ids Nightshift offers and records which request settings are actually served by Nemotron.
meterless_runtime.observed: On 26 Oct 2026 Nightshift often returned HTTP 502; those calls were answered by NVIDIA's API under fallback-nvidia and are counted separately in the README.

meterless_engine.where: H-MEM: app/verdict_memory.py on the gate-1 path (scripts/score_candidates.py, before the trace seal) and app/engines/hmem/ in the evidence-policy track (POST /run). Markovian: app/engines/markovian.py, evidence-policy track only.
meterless_engine.hmem: MemoryStoreService, MemoryRetrievalService and TrustLedgerService, implemented from the published H-MEM spec. Evidence memories are recalled into the judge step; verdicts are promoted to long-term memory and retrieved by type; repeated evidence for the same claim is refreshed, not stacked; superseded memories are kept, not deleted.
meterless_engine.markovian: ChunkManager with a bounded carryover (at most 1200 characters) between agent steps, stopping after 24 chunks.
meterless_engine.tests: tests/engines/test_hmem_spec_model.py (store, ranking formula, promotion, decay, supersede-without-delete) and tests/engines/test_markovian.py, and tests/test_verdict_memory.py for the gate-1 hook, run in CI. They are project tests modelled on the published spec; the official TypeScript conformance suite was not run.
meterless_engine.gate1_hmem: Every gate-1 run writes each verdict to an H-MEM store (<log dir>/hmem/gate1_verdicts.json, ledger gate1_ledger.jsonl) as a long-term memory, recalls the verdicts H-MEM already holds for that repository, supersedes the newest one without deleting it, appends conflict_detected to the trust ledger when they differ, and traces HMEM_VERDICT_MEMORY with verdict_changed. It never changes a verdict; an H-MEM error is traced and the run carries on; PHOENIX_HMEM=off turns it off. The scored 16-repository run predates this hook.

zetaris.role: Gate 1 can read its evidence (phoenix.discovery_candidates, phoenix.prior_art, phoenix.demand_signals) over the REST SQL contract with EVIDENCE_SOURCE=zetaris. Each statement is a trace line with its SQL, query_id and content_hash; a read-only preflight stops the run if Zetaris does not answer.
zetaris.scope: Exercised live and read-only on the 2 repositories in data/real (tharani-2006/Invoice-generator-application, SergioMendolia/ytkb): scripts/zetaris_check.py loads and seals the evidence rows, and a gate-1 run read its evidence from Zetaris. The 16 scored evaluation repositories were fetched live from GitHub with evidence_source=csv.

ai_assistance.tools: Cursor cloud coding agents and Claude (Anthropic), working under the author's direction. The author set the design and rules, reviewed and merged the changes, and ran the live checks.
ai_assistance.product_runtime: The product calls models through Meterless Nightshift, and through NVIDIA's API only under fallback-nvidia. CI never calls a live model or a live Zetaris.

model_mismatch treats a served id as a mismatch unless it starts with nvidia/nemotron-. The direct NVIDIA API once served private/nvidia/nemotron-3.5-super-120b-a12b for the Super-VL id. fallback-nvidia would reject that reply although it is Nemotron. This errs on the safe side: it can wrongly reject a real Nemotron, never accept a non-Nemotron. The rule is unchanged.

On experiment E3, not the scored run, the direct NVIDIA API returned HTTP 429 on 36 of 112 calls across the five runs. The repository's retries completed every call. None failed permanently. That is a rate limit, not a change to the retry code.
